B06-03.question: crane been sitting in the yard since june its october now, its going back out on a construction job. do we need to do anything special before we fire it up and use it
B06-03.note: Question did not say construction or general industry; 1910.180(d)(5) has a different idle-crane rule. Added the construction context.

B20-03.question: hook on our plant's truck crane looks kinda opened up and a lil twisted, at what point is it junk?
B20-03.gold_answer: Under the frequent inspection items for crawler, locomotive and truck cranes, a hook is deficient if it has cracks, a throat opening more than 15 percent over normal, or more than 10° of twist from the plane of the unbent hook. Such a hook is a deficiency to be found in inspection and corrected before the crane is used.

expert_review.why: 1910.180(d)(3)(v) lists the limits as inspection items but does not itself say 'discard'; whether such a hook is junk is field practice.

B08-01.gold_answer: Hand signals do not replace the horn, and a crane with a non-working required horn cannot be operated (safety devices allow no alternative measures). But the horn may be one that is on the equipment and immediately available to the operator, not only a built-in one, so a working horn kept on the crane can satisfy the requirement; the broken built-in horn must be tagged out or removed.

expert_review.why: Whether a handheld air horn kept in the cab is 'on the equipment and immediately available to the operator' is an interpretation.
